faq.title: Top Frequently Asked Questions
faq.caption: Real questions from sales contexts — answers ready to use.

c1.q: How does the pricing model work? Is it a one-time payment or a subscription?
c1.setupDetails: ($500 / $2,000 / $3,250 depending on the plan) paid at signing and non-recurring.
c1.subscriptionDetails: Available in three cycles: quarterly, annual (default), or two years (maximum savings).
c1.note: Single monthly billing is not available; the minimum term is three months.

c2.q: What is the difference between the three plans?
c2.charter: $1,500/year + $500 setup — for Iraq–Iran flight operators. 5 staff accounts in the admin panel.
c2.standard: $4,500/year + $2,000 setup — for full-service travel agencies. Flights + hotels + tours + visas. 15 accounts. Most popular.
c2.advanced: $9,000/year + $3,250 setup — for multi-market operators. Includes iOS and Android apps, insurance, eSIM, 50 accounts, custom domain, and top-priority support.

c3.q: Why an annual subscription and not monthly?
c3.a: Three reasons: (1) Annual gives you a significantly better price. (2) It provides operational stability — no monthly renewals to worry about. (3) The platform powers fixed infrastructure (servers, supplier integrations, licensing); monthly billing would be expensive and impractical for both sides.

c4.q: What is the price difference between the three cycles?
c4.intro: The longer the cycle, the lower the equivalent monthly cost. Example for the Standard plan:

c5.q: Do you take a percentage of my bookings?
c5.a: We do not take a percentage of your booking value. We charge $0.10 per segment applied equally across all services — flights, hotels, visas, insurance, group tours. A segment is counted only on confirmed bookings, not on queries or searches. This fee covers technical processing costs only, not a share of your revenue.

c6.q: What requires additional fees outside the plan?
c6.item1: iOS or Android app ($1,500 setup + $1,200/year) — included in Advanced
c6.item4: Local payment gateways: QiCard / ZainCash / FastPay at $200/year each

c7.q: Do you offer a free trial?
c7.a: No free trial in the traditional sense, but we offer a detailed demo with live screens of all platform flows. For serious prospects, we arrange a hands-on exploration session with their team.

c8.q: Can I upgrade or downgrade my plan later?
c8.upgrade: Yes, at any time and immediately. You pay only the difference on a pro-rated basis for the remaining days plus the setup fee difference. No service interruption.
c8.downgrade: Takes effect at the end of your current paid cycle only. No refund for the difference as the features were already provided.

c9.q: What is the renewal policy? Does it renew automatically?
c9.a: Yes, auto-renewal is enabled by default. The platform sends renewal reminders 30, 14, 7, and 3 days in advance. You can disable auto-renewal manually at least 30 days before the end of your cycle.

c10.q: How long does setup take? When does the subscription period start?
c10.a: We allocate two weeks for onboarding: training, data preparation, supplier connection, and flow testing. The subscription period does not begin until after these two weeks — effectively you get a year and 14 days for the annual price.

c11.q: What is the setup fee refund policy?

t1.q: Which airline suppliers do you integrate with?
t1.a: Through your own supplier accounts. Setup configures the credentials you already hold across your booking channels, so the commercial relationship stays yours — we keep the integrations running. Which channels are available depends on your market, and we go through them with you before you sign.

t2.q: Is the platform hosted by you or do we host it ourselves?
t2.a: Fully hosted by us (SaaS), with daily backups, SSL certificates, and 24/7 monitoring. No setup required on your servers. Self-hosting is available only in custom Enterprise agreements at a separate price.

t3.q: What languages and currencies are supported?
t3.languages: Any language — Arabic, English, French, Persian, Turkish, Kurdish, and more. The interface has full RTL support. Dynamic translations are AI-generated.
t3.currencies: Managed manually by the brand — you add the currencies you want and set exchange rates yourself from the control panel. There is no automatic exchange rate update; you have full control.

t4.a: Yes. The end-client experience (Storefront) is fully responsive and mobile-optimized. Admin panels are desktop-first because they handle dense tables, but they work on tablets and phones. A native mobile app under your brand is available as an add-on — or included in Advanced.

t5.a: QiCard, ZainCash, and FastPay — each as an add-on at $200/year. Additional gateways can be added based on your market.

t6.q: What is the White-Label wallet and why do I need it?
t6.a: A prepaid wallet you top up in advance; it is automatically debited with each API booking. Your margins from each successful booking are added to it. You can withdraw your profits at any time to your bank account. Top-up is available via multiple methods: bank transfer, card, local gateways, and crypto.

o1.q: Do I need a technical team to operate the platform?
o1.a: No. The admin panels are designed for non-technical users. All you need is an operations manager, booking staff, and a marketing team. Anything technical (servers, updates, fixes, supplier management) is handled on our end.

o2.q: Can I grant access to partners or agencies outside my company?
o2.a: No. The platform does not allow granting access to external parties or independent agencies under your brand. What you can do is open internal staff accounts for your company team — each with its own permissions and assigned profit margin — but they operate under your direct management and are not independent entities.

o3.q: What happens if a booking fails after payment?
o3.a: The system initiates an automatic refund, notifies the client, and logs the process in the tracking record. You can intervene as management in exceptional cases.

o4.q: What happens if my wallet balance drops to zero during operations?
o4.a: The platform sends progressive alerts at 80%, 90%, 95%, and 100% depletion. You can enable Auto Top-up to avoid interruption. If the balance runs out, the API pauses temporarily with a generic message to the client — we don't embarrass your brand by showing a financial reason.

o5.q: What if I need a feature that doesn't exist?
o5.a: Some features may be on a near-term roadmap and will reach you automatically through updates. Highly customized features may require a separate custom development agreement. We evaluate cases individually.

d1.q: Who owns the data? Do you share it with other brands?
d1.a: The data is entirely yours — your bookings, your clients, your financial operations. We provide CSV export for any report. Each brand is data-isolated from others with strict permissions. Even we cannot access your data without your consent.

d2.q: What happens to my data when the subscription ends?
d2.grace: Grace period for renewal without data loss
d2.delete: Deletion policy begins — with notification at each stage

d3.q: What happens if Tourscope shuts down?
d3.a: The contract specifies service continuity guarantees. In case of any emergency, we commit to a notice period and safe data transition. All your data remains yours — we provide a full export in CSV/JSON format upon request.

h1.q: What stops me from buying a cheaper system?
h1.a: You can. But compare: does the cheaper system offer real supplier integrations, complex group tours, full visa workflows, insurance, eSIM, multi-currency and multi-language support, hosting and updates, and a prepaid wallet system with automatic financial distribution? And is its interface built to a standard worthy of your brand — or just generic templates that all look the same? Usually not. The cheaper price costs you missing services, manual operations, and a user experience that drives your clients away.

h2.a: WordPress + Plugin = a display product, not an operating system. It doesn't manage sub-agencies, doesn't run real supplier integrations, doesn't manage supplier budgets, doesn't calculate partial refunds, and doesn't support automatic ticketing. It works for a travel blog, not a travel company.

a1.q: Can I cancel the subscription mid-cycle?
a1.a: You can stop auto-renewal, but we do not refund amounts paid for the current period. The subscription continues until the end of the current cycle, then stops.

a2.q: What if I notice a financial discrepancy in my invoices?
a2.a: Our system maintains a complete, immutable audit trail for every operation. Open a ticket through the control panel; the finance team reviews within 48 hours, and if the error is confirmed, we issue a credit note and return the amount to your wallet.

a3.q: Can I view my financial reports at any time?
a3.a: Yes. The wallet panel displays balance, reserved funds, reserves, and revenue in real time. Monthly reports are generated automatically and sent by email, and are exportable as CSV.

hero.heading: The standard behind
hero.subheading: Tourscope wasn't outsourced or templated. It was engineered in-house to one standard — the same standard we hold every line of code to.

pillar1.title: Engineering Quality
pillar1.description: We write code that ages well. Clean architecture, disciplined testing, and an obsession with maintainability are why a platform this large stays fast and changeable instead of becoming a liability.

pillar2.title: Modern UX/UI Systems
pillar2.description: Interfaces that feel intentional. A component-based design system keeps Tourscope consistent across a consumer storefront and a dense operations dashboard — from the first screen to the last.

pillar3.title: Flow-first Thinking
pillar3.description: Complexity is the enemy of adoption. We map every journey — traveler and agent alike — find the friction, and cut steps until booking and back-office work feel effortless.

builds.heading: What that standard ships
builds.b1Desc: Multi-step, multi-role, multi-currency. Built to handle real operational complexity.
builds.b2Desc: Distinct portals for admins, agents, and travelers — all in one coherent system.
builds.b3Desc: Operations-critical interfaces with real-time data and clear decision support.
builds.b4Desc: Multi-tenant, internationalized, and engineered for longevity — not just launch.

cta.heading: Want this engineering standard on your own product?

hero.heading: We are Codescope.
hero.subheading: Disciplined engineering and intentional design, in one team — and a platform in production to prove it.

story.heading: How we got here
story.body: We spent years inside travel agencies, watching capable teams fight broken systems and fragmented suppliers. Most software shops would have built another feature. We built the platform we wished existed — and turned it into Tourscope. Codescope is the company we wanted to work with: technically rigorous, design-conscious, and product-driven.

positioning.label: Where we sit
positioning.statement: Between a software house and a UX agency, you find a product engineering company.
positioning.detail: We don't just execute specs — we challenge them. Every technical decision is a product decision. Every design decision is an engineering decision. We treat them with equal rigour.

hero.headline: The white-label travel platform agencies actually run on.
hero.desc: Tourscope is a complete travel-commerce platform: a marketplace your travelers book on, and a command center your team runs the business from. Six verticals, 15+ supplier integrations, six languages — multi-tenant from the ground up.

twoSides.b2cTitle: Search, compare, and book a whole trip in one place.
twoSides.b2cBody: Flights, hotels, group tours, visas, insurance, and a local eSIM — one fast, beautiful checkout, in the traveler's language and currency.
twoSides.b2bTitle: Run the entire business from one screen.
twoSides.b2bBody: Bookings, suppliers, pricing, payments, and content — managed in a single dashboard, with role-based control over every action.

marketTour.headline: Inside the marketplace.
marketTour.sub: Drawn from the running product — the same fields, the same badges, the same rules.
marketTour.i1Title: One search bar, six products behind it.
marketTour.i1Body: The storefront opens on a single search across flights, hotels, tours, visas, insurance, and eSIMs — in the traveler's language and currency.
marketTour.i2Title: Detail pages that close the sale.
marketTour.i2Body: Prices, processing times, required documents, and the fine print — laid out before the traveler commits, so support doesn't pick up the slack.
marketTour.i3Body: Not a translation layer bolted on — the entire experience mirrors, down to the smallest control.

verticals.headline: Six verticals. One checkout.
verticals.sub: Not a tour widget — a full travel-commerce catalog.
verticals.f1Desc: Round-trip, one-way, and multi-city with live streaming results, branded fares, seat, baggage and meal selection — and per-passenger cancellation handling after the sale.
verticals.f2Desc: Multi-supplier results deduplicated into one catalog, with an interactive price-pin map, rich detail pages, and free-cancellation filters.
verticals.f3Desc: Departure dates, day-by-day itineraries, room and bed selection, and document collection per traveler.
verticals.f4Desc: Apply online by passport and destination, upload documents, and track status after booking.
verticals.f5Desc: Instant quotes, plan comparison, and a PDF policy emailed on purchase.
verticals.f6Desc: A local data plan delivered instantly by QR, with an activation guide.

engine.headline: Everything an agency runs on, in one dashboard.
engine.sub: The back-office most platforms make you buy three separate tools for.
engine.c1I1: Unified booking management across all six verticals, with triage queues — action required, awaiting payment, refunds owed — so nothing waits unseen.
engine.c1I2: Per-passenger and per-leg flight cancellations, manual-recording flows for out-of-band airline work, and refunds routed back to the original payment method.
engine.c1I3: A full support desk: ticket triage, SLA tracking, saved replies, agent performance, and booking-linked threads that update themselves when a booking changes.
engine.c2I1: Every movement is a ledger entry; balances are projections, not editable numbers.
engine.c2I2: Deposits, earnings with holdback windows, supplier balances, and payout requests.
engine.c2I3: Branded account statements — PDF and Excel — whose closing balance always reconciles.
engine.c2I4: Markups, commissions, buyer-group pricing tiers, cancellation penalties, and exchange-rate control.
engine.c3I1: A cross-agency inventory pool: share your visas, tours, hotels, and charter seats with partner agencies — or resell theirs — with clean settlement between both sides.
engine.c3I2: A charter marketplace — curated routes and seats from regional operators.
engine.c3I3: A Partner API so integrators can search and book against your inventory from their own systems.
engine.c4I1: White-label branding: logo, colors, hero galleries, languages, and currencies.
engine.c4I2: A block-based CMS: articles in multiple languages, FAQs, city pages, and promotions.
engine.c4I3: Role-based access for staff, corporate company accounts with wallets and credit, and per-customer pricing tiers.

beyond.headline: And the parts you only notice later.
beyond.sub: The features that don't fit a comparison table — until you run an agency on them.
beyond.b1Body: Give corporate clients their own accounts: staff seats, shared wallets, credit limits, and statements — while you keep control of pricing.
beyond.b2Body: Tier your customers into buyer groups and let the platform price each one automatically — retail, corporate, partner.
beyond.b3Body: Tickets link to bookings, track SLAs, and update themselves when the booking changes — with saved replies and agent performance built in.
beyond.b4Body: Confirmations, vouchers, cancellations, and account statements go out from your identity — in the customer's language.
beyond.b5Body: Hotel descriptions translate with AI assistance; your own articles and pages publish per language from one editor.
beyond.b6Body: Live booking queues, revenue summaries, and per-vertical performance — the day's state of the business at a glance.
